text: And that's why people have filed amicus briefs and are very concerned.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: But more to the point, these things have not moved under the riverbed recently.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: They've been sitting there for 100 years, and the State lent its eminent domain power to us to help us build these dams.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: These dams were critical to developing energy and development in this area.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: And now 100 years later, they want compensation for the little river strip--

speaker: Antonin Scalia
text: Could the United States demand compensation?

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: --We pay the United States compensation right now.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: The difference is, the United States isn't going in afterwards and trying to put a hold-up to us and saying it wants $50 million for this.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: We pay rents to FERC for some of these lands.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Actually, the State gets 37.5 percent of the--

speaker: Antonin Scalia
text: For the riverbed?

speaker: Antonin Scalia
text: For the riverbed land?

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: --Well, look at footnote 3 of the government's brief.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: I mean, again, the problem here is if you want people to have deeds that really are -- parse out whether it's riverbed or upland, they don't because everybody defaults to the bottom line -- the background rule.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: The background rule is if it's a non-navigable river, the riparian owners, whether it be the United States or private property owners, get to midway, or if they own both on both sides, they get the whole thing.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: I think on de minimis, we've talked about it a lot.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: But I would point out that the one thing we know that is not de minimis from Utah is 4.35 miles.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Because that's what the Court analyzed separately in the portion of Cataract Canyon.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Every stretch at issue here, every dam at issue here, is more than 4.35 miles.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Fully five of the dams are on the 17-mile Great Falls stretch, which they agree is impassable.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: The other five are reservoir dams that create reservoirs that extend over 4.35 miles.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: There's nothing de minimis in the best evidence that is the $50 million in compensation.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: I think the $50 million in background also shows that although this is a dispute between Montana and the United States, my client is caught in the middle of it, and they are obviously concerned about it, too.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: I want to talk about what's disputed and what's undisputed.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: What is undisputed is the 17 miles is impassable.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: That's enough, as I say, to give us judgment as a matter of law for the five dams on that stretch.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: What is hotly disputed, despite my friend's representation, is whether or not there was through commerce through this bypass route.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: He suggests it's undisputed that gold went from Helena down to Fort Benton down to St. Louis.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: And that of course is not disputed.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: But it went on roads.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: It didn't go on the upper Missouri.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: And if you want to know who's got the better of this argument, I ask you to think about this question: the United States Army built a 600-mile overland road from Fort Benton, the traditional head of navigation on the Missouri, to Walla Walla, Washington.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Now, if the State is right and the upper Missouri and the Clark Fork were navigable, all they had to do was have a 60-mile road to connect the two.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: They were never navigable.

speaker: Paul D. Clement
text: Thank you, Your Honor.

speaker: John G. Roberts, Jr.
text: Thank you, counsel.

speaker: John G. Roberts, Jr.
text: The case is now submitted.
